137	// between a query and appends. Must be closed when complete.
138	func (i *isolation) State(mint, maxt int64) *isolationState {
139		i.appendMtx.RLock() // Take append mutex before read mutex.
140		defer i.appendMtx.RUnlock()
141	
142		// We need to track reads even when isolation is disabled, so that head
143		// truncation can wait till reads overlapping that range have finished.
144		isoState := &isolationState{
145			maxAppendID:       i.appendsOpenList.appendID,
146			lowWatermark:      i.appendsOpenList.next.appendID, // Lowest appendID from appenders, or lastAppendId.
147			incompleteAppends: make(map[uint64]struct{}, len(i.appendsOpen)),
148			isolation:         i,
149			mint:              mint,
150			maxt:              maxt,
151		}
152		for k := range i.appendsOpen {
153			isoState.incompleteAppends[k] = struct{}{}
154		}
155	
156		i.readMtx.Lock()
157		defer i.readMtx.Unlock()
158		isoState.prev = i.readsOpen
159		isoState.next = i.readsOpen.next
160		i.readsOpen.next.prev = isoState
161		i.readsOpen.next = isoState
162	
163		return isoState
164	}

166	// TraverseOpenReads iterates through the open reads and runs the given
167	// function on those states. The given function MUST NOT mutate the isolationState.
168	// The iteration is stopped when the function returns false or once all reads have been iterated.
169	func (i *isolation) TraverseOpenReads(f func(s *isolationState) bool) {
170		i.readMtx.RLock()
171		defer i.readMtx.RUnlock()
172		s := i.readsOpen.next
173		for s != i.readsOpen {
174			if !f(s) {
175				return
176			}
177			s = s.next
178		}
179	}

183	// Also returns the low watermark, to keep lock/unlock operations down.
184	func (i *isolation) newAppendID(minTime int64) (uint64, uint64) {
185		if i.disabled {
186			return 0, 0
187		}
188	
189		i.appendMtx.Lock()
190		defer i.appendMtx.Unlock()
191	
192		// Last used appendID is stored in head element.
193		i.appendsOpenList.appendID++
194	
195		app := i.appendersPool.Get().(*isolationAppender)
196		app.appendID = i.appendsOpenList.appendID
197		app.minTime = minTime
198		app.prev = i.appendsOpenList.prev
199		app.next = i.appendsOpenList
200	
201		i.appendsOpenList.prev.next = app
202		i.appendsOpenList.prev = app
203	
204		i.appendsOpen[app.appendID] = app
205		return app.appendID, i.lowWatermarkLocked()
206	}

input.reason: The watermark is read with `iso.lastAppendID()` (db.go:1745) before any blocks are written. In Prometheus, an appender gets its appendID when it is created (`newAppendID`), not when it commits. So take an appender opened before the watermark is read but committed after the block writer took its isolation snapshot. Its appendID is <= the watermark, and it was still in `incompleteAppends` during the write, so its samples are left out of the block. If it commits before eviction, its txs entry is <= the watermark, so `hasAppendIDAbove` returns false. The sample's timestamp is <= maxt, so gcSeries does not keep the series either. The series is evicted and a WAL tombstone is written, so that committed sample is permanently lost, even with isolation enabled. This also breaks the code's own claim that blocks contain "all samples with appendID <= watermark". Using the low watermark, or checking against open appenders, would close the gap. The race window is narrow, but when it hits, acknowledged data is silently lost.
